title: UNIONS v2, four tomographic bins (blinded data)
stale_note: This run predates the recalibrated n(z) bins of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468; the remeasurement on the new bins is running.
summary: Jointly over all ten bin pairs, Cℓ EB, COSEBIs B, ξ₊ᴮ and 2–20′ ξ±ᴮ pass; Cℓ BB, ξ₋ᴮ and ξ±ᴮ combined fail (PTE < 0.05).
banner: Blinded (blind: unions): E-mode data vectors are concealed; do not interpret cosmology
provenance: ShapePipe SP v2.0, size bound 9; 170.6M galaxies on 19,940 tiles, 4,690 deg²; tomographic footprint (tiles with z-band photometry) 15,830 tiles, 3,815 deg²
first working DR6 BPZ+SOM four-bin n(z), validation and null tests only (not the recalibrated n(z) of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468); ⟨z⟩ = 0.286, 0.448, 0.612, 0.929
headline_note: PTE of each B-mode null test, jointly over the ten bin pairs

tables.caption: Probability to exceed (PTE) the measured χ² if the B modes are zero, for each bin pair and jointly over all ten pairs. Scale cuts: COSEBIs modes n ≤ 20 and pure-mode ξ±ᴮ at 12–83′; pseudo-Cℓ over all 32 bandpowers; the small-scale test is pure-mode ξ±ᴮ at 2–20′. Real-space covariance: OneCovariance (analytic); pseudo-Cℓ covariance: Gaussian (NaMaster). Values below 0.05 are failures.

rows.label: joint
rows.note: all ten pairs, full cross-pair covariance

figures.caption: PTE of each B-mode null test for every pair of the four tomographic bins. Blue cells are below 0.05; dark red cells are above 0.95, which would point to an overestimated covariance. Each panel title gives the joint PTE over all ten pairs.
figures.alt: PTE of each B-mode null test for every pair of the four tomographic bins. Blue cells are below 0.05; dark red cells are above 0.95, which would point to an overestimated covariance. Each panel title gives the joint PTE over all ten pairs.

figures.caption: Pure-mode B-mode correlation functions ξ₊ᴮ (circles) and ξ₋ᴮ (squares) for each bin pair, with errors from the analytic covariance. Shaded scales lie outside the 12–83′ range of the test; each panel prints its PTEs.
figures.alt: Pure-mode B-mode correlation functions ξ₊ᴮ (circles) and ξ₋ᴮ (squares) for each bin pair, with errors from the analytic covariance. Shaded scales lie outside the 12–83′ range of the test; each panel prints its PTEs.

figures.caption: COSEBIs B modes Bₙ (n ≤ 20, 12–83′) for each bin pair, in units of their own standard deviation, with bands at ±1σ and ±2σ. The modes are correlated, so judge by the PTE rather than by single points.
figures.alt: COSEBIs B modes Bₙ (n ≤ 20, 12–83′) for each bin pair, in units of their own standard deviation, with bands at ±1σ and ±2σ. The modes are correlated, so judge by the PTE rather than by single points.

figures.caption: Pseudo-Cℓ BB (circles) and EB (squares) for each bin pair, with a Gaussian NaMaster covariance built on each bin's own map and mask. The PTEs use all 32 bandpowers.
figures.alt: Pseudo-Cℓ BB (circles) and EB (squares) for each bin pair, with a Gaussian NaMaster covariance built on each bin's own map and mask. The PTEs use all 32 bandpowers.

figures.caption: Whole-sample ξ±ᴮ as measured (points) and after masking six objects that contaminated the PSF star sample (M33, M101, M13, M92, Draco, Ursa Minor; crosses): no point moves by more than 0.06σ. This test comes from an earlier non-tomographic run on 138M galaxies, not from this run.
figures.alt: Whole-sample ξ±ᴮ as measured (points) and after masking six objects that contaminated the PSF star sample (M33, M101, M13, M92, Draco, Ursa Minor; crosses): no point moves by more than 0.06σ. This test comes from an earlier non-tomographic run on 138M galaxies, not from this run.

figures.caption: Blinded θξ₊ and θξ₋ for each bin pair against a Planck 2018 prediction without intrinsic alignments. The band shows how far the blinding can move the data (S₈ ± 0.075, Ωₘ ± 0.1); it can raise ξ₊ above about 50′ by up to a factor of two in the high-redshift pairs, so such a rise is not by itself a systematic.
figures.alt: Blinded θξ₊ and θξ₋ for each bin pair against a Planck 2018 prediction without intrinsic alignments. The band shows how far the blinding can move the data (S₈ ± 0.075, Ωₘ ± 0.1); it can raise ξ₊ above about 50′ by up to a factor of two in the high-redshift pairs, so such a rise is not by itself a systematic.

figures.caption: Blinded pseudo-Cℓ EE for each bin pair against the fiducial prediction convolved with each band's window.
figures.alt: Blinded pseudo-Cℓ EE for each bin pair against the fiducial prediction convolved with each band's window.

figures.caption: Blinded consistency test: one template amplitude per bin pair, fitted jointly to ξ± at 5–100′ and shown relative to the common amplitude; the χ² tests whether all ten pairs share one amplitude. Grey: template without intrinsic alignments; blue: with NLA alignments (A_IA = 1); red: NLA after subtracting the PSF-leakage term from the data. The test was designed after seeing the blinded data.
figures.alt: Blinded consistency test: one template amplitude per bin pair, fitted jointly to ξ± at 5–100′ and shown relative to the common amplitude; the χ² tests whether all ten pairs share one amplitude. Grey: template without intrinsic alignments; blue: with NLA alignments (A_IA = 1); red: NLA after subtracting the PSF-leakage term from the data. The test was designed after seeing the blinded data.

figures.caption: ρ statistics of the PSF stars, which measure the PSF model residuals; all four bins share them.
figures.alt: ρ statistics of the PSF stars, which measure the PSF model residuals; all four bins share them.

figures.caption: τ₀, τ₂ and τ₅ (correlations between galaxy shapes and PSF quantities) for each tomographic bin, with each bin's fitted leakage model as lines.
figures.alt: τ₀, τ₂ and τ₅ (correlations between galaxy shapes and PSF quantities) for each tomographic bin, with each bin's fitted leakage model as lines.

figures.caption: PSF-leakage coefficients α, β and η per bin, from a fit of the τ statistics to the ρ templates with ρ held fixed. The τ estimator biases α low by about 25% on a simulation with known leakage (CosmoStat/shear_psf_leakage#58), so read these α as lower limits.
figures.alt: PSF-leakage coefficients α, β and η per bin, from a fit of the τ statistics to the ρ templates with ρ held fixed. The τ estimator biases α low by about 25% on a simulation with known leakage (CosmoStat/shear_psf_leakage#58), so read these α as lower limits.

figures.caption: The four-bin redshift distributions of this run: first working DR6 BPZ+SOM four-bin n(z), validation and null tests only (not the recalibrated n(z) of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468).
figures.alt: The four-bin redshift distributions of this run: first working DR6 BPZ+SOM four-bin n(z), validation and null tests only (not the recalibrated n(z) of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468).

figures.caption: Analytic (OneCovariance) ξ± variance divided by the data's 100-patch jackknife variance, per bin pair (auto-correlations coloured, cross-correlations grey); the band is the jackknife's own ±14% scatter. The median ratio is 1.08 below 10′ (required within 15% of 1) and 1.03 at 12–83′.
